## Purpose and status

This is an internal `fplida` explainer for the Single Touch Payroll (STP)
dataset. It records what the synthetic STP products are intended to
represent, how the main variables should be interpreted, and which source
documents justify those interpretations. It is deliberately stored under
`inst/internal-docs/` rather than `vignettes/` so it is available inside the
package source and installed package, but is not yet promoted as a user-facing
vignette.

The current STP implementation follows the 19 March 2026 PLIDA Data Item List
(DIL) shape. It emits STP as raw DIL-style products only. It does not create a
derived weekly earnings table and it does not add variables that are not in the
STP product metadata. Downstream weekly, person-week, or main-job measures
should be derived outside the STP generator from the raw extended pay-event
tables.

## Source documents

The interpretation in this note is based on these source classes.

1. Local PLIDA metadata:

   - `inst/plida_metadata/variables.csv`
   - `data-raw/PLIDA data item list - 19MAR2026.xlsx`

   These files define the STP product names, table names, variable names, and
   local variable descriptions that the generator must match.

2. Local generator and tests:

   - `R/generate_stp.R`
   - `src/rust/src/stp.rs`
   - `tests/testthat/test-dil-2026.R`

   These are the current implementation and regression checks.

3. ATO Phase 1 STP source material:

   - [ATO Single Touch Payroll overview](https://softwaredevelopers.ato.gov.au/STP)
   - [ATO Payroll Event Data Definitions v0.012](https://softwaredevelopers.ato.gov.au/sites/default/files/resource-attachments/DWG_17_11_Payroll_Event_Data_Definitions_v.012.pdf)
   - [ATO rules of reporting through STP](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/single-touch-payroll/in-detail/single-touch-payroll-employer-reporting-guidelines/rules-of-reporting-through-stp)

   The ATO overview describes STP as payroll reporting of salaries and wages,
   PAYG withholding, and super information at the time employers pay employees.
   The Phase 1 payroll event data definitions are the core source for the
   meaning of Phase 1 pay-event fields, including gross payments, allowances,
   withholding, reportable fringe benefits, foreign employment fields,
   personal-services income fields, and employment termination payments.

4. ATO Phase 2 contrast documents:

   - [ATO STP Phase 2 position paper](https://softwaredevelopers.ato.gov.au/sites/default/files/resource-attachments/ATO_STP_Phase_2_Position_Paper_V1.1_Final_clean.pdf)
   - [ATO STP Phase 2 income types and country codes position paper](https://softwaredevelopers.ato.gov.au/sites/default/files/resource-attachments/ATO_STP_Phase_2_Income_Types-Country_Codes_Position_Paper_v1.0.pdf)
   - [ATO Phase 2 disaggregation of gross](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/single-touch-payroll/in-detail/single-touch-payroll-phase-2-employer-reporting-guidelines/reporting-the-amounts-you-have-paid/disaggregation-of-gross)
   - [ATO Phase 2 payments you must report](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/single-touch-payroll/in-detail/single-touch-payroll-phase-2-employer-reporting-guidelines/payments-you-must-report)
   - [ATO Phase 2 other components of STP reporting](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/single-touch-payroll/in-detail/single-touch-payroll-phase-2-employer-reporting-guidelines/other-components-of-your-stp-reporting)

   These are used only as contrast documents. They describe extra Phase 2
   disaggregation and income-type reporting, so they help identify what Phase 1
   style variables do not separately observe. They are not evidence that the
   local DIL STP product contains Phase 2 fields.

5. Tax and earnings concept sources:

   - [ATO PAYG withholding schedule for back payments, commissions, bonuses and similar payments](https://softwaredevelopers.ato.gov.au/sites/default/files/resource-attachments/NAT3348-05-2013_tax_table_for_back_payments_commissions_bonuses_and_similar_payments_0.pdf)
   - [ABS Average Weekly Earnings methodology, November 2025](https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/average-weekly-earnings-australia-methodology/nov-2025)
   - [ABS Employee Earnings and Hours methodology, May 2025](https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/employee-earnings-and-hours-australia-methodology/may-2025)
   - [ABS Characteristics of Employment methodology, August 2025](https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/characteristics-employment-australia-methodology/aug-2025)

   These sources clarify the distinction between STP pay-event amounts and
   ABS earnings concepts such as ordinary-time earnings, total earnings, hours,
   full-time status, main job, and multiple jobholding.

## Source-backed coverage decisions

| Product area | What the research source supports | What is still not found |
|---|---|---|
| DIL-shaped STP schema | Local PLIDA metadata proves the generated STP variable names and product/table names used in this package. The representative generated schema has direct metadata matches for all 92 observed STP rows. | Public ATO pages do not prove the local DIL column names one-for-one; use local DIL metadata for exact schema and ATO pages for reporting semantics. |
| Gross pay and PAYG withholding | ATO STP reporting rules support reporting period gross salary/wages and PAYG withholding through pay events. | I did not find public evidence that `INCM_GRS_AMT` and `PMT_SUMRY_TOTL_GRS_PMT_AMT` should always be equal; their equality is current local generator behaviour only. |
| Phase 1 versus Phase 2 payment detail | ATO Phase 2 guidance supports the distinction that Phase 2 disaggregates gross into more separately itemised components. | The current local STP product should not be described as observing Phase 2 bonus, overtime, paid-leave, salary-sacrifice, or hours variables unless those DIL fields are actually present. |
| Earnings concepts | ABS AWE/EEH/Characteristics of Employment methodologies support the warning that survey earnings concepts differ from raw STP pay-event fields. | I did not find a source that makes STP pay-event gross equivalent to AWOTE, OTE, hourly wages, or full-time adult ordinary-time earnings. |

## Product structure

The 2026 DIL exposes STP through two products:

| Product | Role in fplida |
|---|---|
| `pmp-stp-standard` | Standard STP pay-event and job tables. Kept for DIL shape coverage and compatibility. |
| `pmp-stp-extended` | Extended STP pay-event, job, and employment termination payment tables. This is the preferred source for downstream labour-market derivations. |

The generator writes these products under `ato-stp/`.

### Pay-event tables

Pay-event tables are monthly. For DIL years 2020 to 2024, the generator emits
January to December. For 2025, it emits January to October, matching the
current DIL range.

Examples:

- `stp_standard_pay_events_2020_m01`
- `stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m01`
- `stp_standard_pay_events_2025_m10`
- `stp_extended_pay_events_2025_m10`

The standard pay-event tables have 20 variables. The extended pay-event tables
have 50 variables. The extended variables include all standard fields plus
additional income-type, lump-sum, withholding, fringe-benefit, geography, and
termination fields.

### Jobs tables

Jobs tables are financial-year tables.

Examples:

- `stp_standard_jobs_2019_20`
- `stp_extended_jobs_2019_20`
- `stp_standard_jobs_2025_26`
- `stp_extended_jobs_2025_26`

The jobs tables contain only the payer, person, payroll financial year,
relationship commencement date, and relationship cessation date. They are a
thin job-relationship layer, not a full employment history table.

### ETP tables

Employment termination payment (ETP) tables are present in the extended
product only.

Examples:

- `stp_extended_etp_2019_20`
- `stp_extended_etp_2025_26`

ETP rows are generated only for a subset of ended jobs. The ETP table is the
place for employment termination payment components; these amounts should not
be re-created in pay-event gross or lump-sum fields unless the source product
has a separate pay-event field for that concept.

### File format

STP is parquet-only in `fplida`. `generate_stp()` rejects CSV output. This is
intentional because the STP DIL products are large, table-based, and consumed
efficiently through parquet-backed pipelines.

## Variable-level schema register

Every generated variable observed in this pass for this guide is listed in
[`schema-registers/schema-register-stp.csv`](schema-registers/schema-register-stp.csv).
The register records R type, sampled generated missingness, sampled generated
domains/distributions, and direct PLIDA metadata matches. Treat those sampled
domains/distributions as implementation evidence only, not as official ATO STP
payroll data.

A rendered variable evidence appendix for this guide is available at [`variable-evidence-appendices/stp-variable-evidence.qmd`](variable-evidence-appendices/stp-variable-evidence.qmd). It contains one row per generated variable with observed generated values or distributions, local metadata/crosswalk status, and unresolved-source caveats.

| Dataset | Generated variable rows | Direct PLIDA metadata matches | No direct PLIDA name match |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `STP` | 92 | 92 | 0 |

The direct matches mean the representative generated STP columns align by name
with local PLIDA metadata. Payroll-event semantics, reporting rules, and code

before use as source-data facts.

## Core design principle

The generator must preserve the distinction between observed raw STP fields and
derived labour-market measures.

The raw STP products should contain only variables that exist in the DIL STP
metadata. Derived variables such as person-week earnings, regular earnings,
main-job earnings, payment shocks, or AWE-like aggregates should be computed by
downstream code from the extended raw tables.

The generator should still create realistic synthetic behaviour. It currently
does this through:

- deterministic job histories;
- zero, positive, and negative gaps between jobs;
- mostly fortnightly pay periods, with smaller monthly and weekly shares;
- a chaotic tail of irregular and overlapping pay periods;
- occasional financial-year-anchored long periods;
- irregular gross-payment spikes, concentrated around June;
- rare overpayment rows followed by negative correction rows.

Those behavioural features should be represented using real STP variables.
They should not require invented columns or semantic misuse of existing fields.

## Phase 1 versus Phase 2

The local STP pay-event product is treated as Phase 1 style STP. That is the
central constraint.

Phase 1 reports payroll information using broad payment-summary style
categories. For ordinary salary and wage employees, the core pay-event amount
is gross salary and wages. Bonuses and commissions can be part of this gross
amount, but Phase 1 does not provide a separate observed bonus or commission
field.

Phase 2 introduced more disaggregated payment types, including separately
identified bonuses and commissions, overtime, directors' fees, paid leave, and
salary sacrifice. Those Phase 2 additions are useful for understanding what is
missing from Phase 1, but they should not be back-filled into this STP product.

Practical implications:

- `INCM_GRS_AMT` can represent gross salary and wages for a pay event.
- `PMT_SUMRY_TOTL_GRS_PMT_AMT` can be used as the headline gross payment and a
  reconciliation column.
- End-of-financial-year irregular synthetic payments belong inside gross
  payment amounts.
- There is no raw `bonus`, `commission`, `overtime`, `ordinary_time`, or
  `hours` variable in the current STP product.
- Do not infer an observed bonus by looking for spikes. A spike can be used as
  a derived irregular-payment proxy, but it is not an observed bonus field.

## Variable groups

This section uses lower-case names when discussing concepts and upper-case names
when naming raw columns exactly as they appear in generated output.

### Keys and identifiers

| Variable | Meaning and use | Current fplida treatment |
|---|---|---|
| `SYNTHETIC_AEUID` | Person identifier. This is the main key for person-level analysis. | Comes from the ATO person identifier on the synthetic spine. |
| `BN` | Confidentialised business identifier for the payer. Useful as an employer or payer key, but not necessarily a workplace or site. | Deterministically generated per synthetic job. |
| `BRANCH_NUMBER` | Employer branch number. Branch numbers represent subdivisions for tax obligations. | Deterministic small integer derived from person and job. |
| `EMPLOYEE_KEY` | Encrypted ID unique to a job. Useful for job-like analysis. | Built from person and payer identifiers. |
| `SEQUENCE_KEY` | Encrypted ID unique to a job pay sequence. Useful for distinguishing multiple pay-event rows under one job. | Includes year, month, job number, pay-period sequence, and correction/overpayment suffixes when relevant. |
| `CNTRCTR_BN` | Contractor client identifier. Relevant for contractor-style streams such as voluntary agreements. | Left missing because the current ordinary employee generator does not model contractor-client streams. |
| `DUMMY_FLAG` | Synthetic/dummy identifier flag. | Set to `"False"` in generated rows. |

`CNTRCTR_BN` should stay blank unless the generator actually creates a
contractor-style income stream. Filling it randomly on ordinary wage rows would
misrepresent the income type.

### Dates and relationship fields

| Variable | Meaning and use | Current fplida treatment |
|---|---|---|
| `DRVPAYSTARTDATE` | Derived start date for the pay-event period. | Start of the synthetic pay period, clamped to the job relationship. |
| `DRVPAYENDDATE` | Derived end date for the pay-event period. | End of the synthetic pay period, clamped to the job relationship. |
| `PMT_DT` | Payment date. | Payment date for the event, usually near period end but not identical to the worked-period dates. |
| `PYRL_FNCL_YR` | Payroll financial year. | Derived from the pay event month. |
| `PYR_PYE_RLTNSHP_CMNCMT_DT` | Payer-payee relationship commencement date. | Synthetic job start date. |
| `PYR_PYE_RLTNSHP_CESTN_DT` | Payer-payee relationship cessation date. | Present when a job ends within the relevant pay period or financial year. |
| `PYR_PYE_RLTNSHP_TRMNTD_IND` | Relationship terminated indicator. | Set to 1 on extended pay-event rows when a cessation date is present, otherwise 0. |

For accrual-style labour-market measures, allocate amounts across
`DRVPAYSTARTDATE` to `DRVPAYENDDATE`. For payment-week or cash-flow measures,
use `PMT_DT`.

### Gross pay and allowances

| Variable | Meaning | Current fplida treatment |
|---|---|---|
| `INCM_GRS_AMT` | Gross amount of salary and wages income for the event. | Equal to the synthetic event gross payment. Includes irregular gross-payment spikes when generated. |
| `PMT_SUMRY_TOTL_GRS_PMT_AMT` | Total amount of gross payments for the event. | Equal to `INCM_GRS_AMT` in current synthetic ordinary employee rows. Kept as a separate raw reconciliation field. |
| `ALWNC_INCM_TOTL_AMT` | Allowance income total amount for the event. | Separate from gross. Some jobs receive a deterministic allowance amount. |

Recommended downstream component names:

```r
gross_salary_wages = coalesce(INCM_GRS_AMT, 0)
gross_payment_summary = coalesce(PMT_SUMRY_TOTL_GRS_PMT_AMT, 0)
allowances = coalesce(ALWNC_INCM_TOTL_AMT, 0)
gross_plus_allowances = gross_salary_wages + allowances
```

Do not add `INCM_GRS_AMT` and `PMT_SUMRY_TOTL_GRS_PMT_AMT` together. In the
current generator they are the same ordinary gross amount, represented in two
raw fields that have different reporting labels.

### Bonuses, commissions, and irregular payments

There is no observed Phase 1 bonus or commission field in this STP product.
The generator therefore does not create a bonus column and does not store
synthetic bonus-like behaviour in lump-sum fields.

The current generator creates irregular gross-payment spikes. These are useful
for testing weekly calendarisation and payment-shock logic. They are included
inside `INCM_GRS_AMT` and `PMT_SUMRY_TOTL_GRS_PMT_AMT`, which is consistent
with Phase 1 gross-pay reporting.

Valid downstream labels:

- `irregular_gross_payment_proxy`
- `gross_payment_spike`
- `payment_week_shock`

Invalid downstream labels for Phase 1 data:

- `bonus`
- `commission`
- `overtime`
- `ordinary_time_earnings`
- `AWOTE`

### Lump sums A, B, D, and E

| Variable | Meaning | Current fplida treatment |
|---|---|---|
| `ANL_LNG_SRVC_UNSD_LS_A_AMT` | Lump sum A amount, generally related to unused annual leave, unused long-service leave, and related leave payments. | Generated only on a subset of final-pay rows where a cessation date is present. |
| `ANL_LNG_SRVC_UNSD_LS_A_CD` | Lump sum A code. Phase 1 definitions use codes such as `R` and `T` to distinguish redundancy/retirement-linked cases from other cases. | `R` or `T` when lump sum A is positive; missing otherwise. |
| `ANL_LNG_SRVC_UNSD_LS_B_AMT` | Lump sum B amount, unused long-service leave accrued before 16 August 1978. | Currently zero. |
| `ANL_LNG_SRVC_UNSD_LS_D_AMT` | Lump sum D amount, tax-free genuine redundancy or early retirement payment below the tax-free threshold. | Currently zero. |
| `ANL_LNG_SRVC_UNSD_LS_E_AMT` | Lump sum E amount, back payment of certain amounts accrued more than 12 months ago. | Currently zero. |

Lump sum A should not be used as a bonus proxy. Its current synthetic role is a
final-pay leave payout. That keeps the raw field meaning close to the ATO
Phase 1 definitions while still giving downstream pipelines realistic
non-regular final-payment behaviour to handle.

Recommended downstream components:

```r
leave_lump_sum_a = coalesce(ANL_LNG_SRVC_UNSD_LS_A_AMT, 0)
leave_lump_sum_b = coalesce(ANL_LNG_SRVC_UNSD_LS_B_AMT, 0)
leave_lump_sum = leave_lump_sum_a + leave_lump_sum_b
redundancy_lump_sum = coalesce(ANL_LNG_SRVC_UNSD_LS_D_AMT, 0)
backpay_lump_sum = coalesce(ANL_LNG_SRVC_UNSD_LS_E_AMT, 0)
lump_sum_total = leave_lump_sum + redundancy_lump_sum + backpay_lump_sum
has_lump_sum = lump_sum_total > 0
```

### Special income streams

| Variable | Meaning | Current fplida treatment |
|---|---|---|
| `INCM_LABR_HIR_ARNGMT_GRS_AMT` | Labour-hire arrangement gross amount. | Zero unless a labour-hire stream is explicitly modelled. |
| `LABR_HIR_TOTL_AMT` | Labour-hire total PAYGW amount. | Zero unless a labour-hire stream is explicitly modelled. |
| `INCM_VA_GRS_AMT` | Voluntary agreement gross amount. | Zero unless a voluntary agreement stream is explicitly modelled. |
| `VA_TOTL_AMT` | Voluntary agreement total PAYGW amount. | Zero unless a voluntary agreement stream is explicitly modelled. |
| `INCM_WHM_GRS_AMT` | Working holiday maker gross amount. | Zero unless a WHM stream is explicitly modelled. |
| `WHM_TOTL_AMT` | Working holiday maker total PAYGW amount. | Zero unless a WHM stream is explicitly modelled. |
| `INCM_CMNTY_DEV_EMPLT_PRJCT_AMT` | Community Development Employment Project amount. | Zero unless a CDEP stream is explicitly modelled. |
| `OTHR_SPCFD_TOTL_AMT` | Other specified payments total amount. | Zero unless an other specified payment stream is explicitly modelled. |
| `INCM_OTHR_AMT` | Other income amount. | Zero unless an other-income stream is explicitly modelled. |

These fields identify special or non-standard income streams. They should not
be silently mixed into ordinary salary and wage measures. If future generator
work models these streams, it should also set the corresponding identifiers,
withholding fields, and validation tests consistently.

Recommended broad special-income component:

```r
special_income_total =
  coalesce(INCM_LABR_HIR_ARNGMT_GRS_AMT, 0) +
  coalesce(INCM_VA_GRS_AMT, 0) +
  coalesce(INCM_WHM_GRS_AMT, 0) +
  coalesce(INCM_CMNTY_DEV_EMPLT_PRJCT_AMT, 0) +
  coalesce(OTHR_SPCFD_TOTL_AMT, 0) +
  coalesce(INCM_OTHR_AMT, 0)
```

### Foreign employment fields

| Variable | Meaning | Current fplida treatment |
|---|---|---|
| `F_EMPLT_INCM_GRS_AMT` | Foreign employment income gross amount. | Zero for ordinary domestic wage rows. |
| `F_EMPLT_INCM_TOTL_AMT` | Foreign employment income total amount. | Zero for ordinary domestic wage rows. |
| `F_EMPLT_INCM_JPDA_GRS_AMT` | Foreign employment JPDA gross amount. | Zero. |
| `F_EMPLT_INCM_JPDA_TOTL_AMT` | Foreign employment JPDA total amount. | Zero. |
| `F_INCM_EXMT_AMT` | Foreign income exempt amount. | Zero. |
| `F_EMPLT_INCM_TAX_CR_WHELD_AMT` | Foreign income employment tax credit withheld amount. | Zero for ordinary domestic wage rows. |
| `F_EMPLT_INCM_TAX_PMT_AMT` | Foreign employment income total taxed amount. | Zero for ordinary domestic wage rows. |

These fields should not mirror ordinary domestic gross pay. If they are used in
the future, they should represent an explicitly modelled foreign employment
stream. This avoids falsely flagging ordinary wage rows as foreign-employment
income.

### Withholding, deductions, super, and fringe benefits

| Variable | Meaning | Current fplida treatment |
|---|---|---|
| `TAX_WHELD_TOTL_AMT` | Total PAYG withholding for the event. | Synthetic event-level withholding. Negative corrections can have negative withholding. |
| `WHELD_AMT` | Locally labelled as year-to-date withheld amount - event payment. | Equal to `TAX_WHELD_TOTL_AMT` in current synthetic output. This is a simplification to be validated if real data use requires the distinction. |
| `IDV_WRKPLC_GVING_TOTL_AMT` | Workplace giving amount. | Occasional small positive amount on ordinary positive-payment rows. |
| `SG_EMPLR_CNTRBTN_AMT` | Super guarantee employer contribution amount. | Generated from gross using the applicable synthetic SG rate for the payroll financial year. |
| `PYR_SPNTN_CNTRBTN_RPRTBL_AMT` | Reportable employer superannuation contribution amount. | Generated for a subset of jobs. |
| `RFB_EXMT_AMT` | Reportable fringe benefits exempt amount. | Currently zero. |
| `RFB_TXBL_AMT` | Reportable fringe benefits taxable amount. | Currently zero. |

Super and reportable fringe benefits are not cash weekly earnings and should
not be used as AWE or AWOTE components. They can be used for broader
remuneration or labour-cost sensitivity checks when labelled explicitly.

### Geography and demographics

| Variable | Meaning | Current fplida treatment |
|---|---|---|
| `BIRTH_YEAR_MONTH_ABS` | Month and year of payee date of birth. | Derived from spine year of birth plus deterministic month. |
| `STATE_ASGS_2021` | State code. | Comes from the synthetic spine state. |
| `SA2_ASGS_2021` | Geocoded SA2. | Deterministic state/person-based code. |
| `LGA_ASGS_2022` | Geocoded LGA. | Deterministic row-based code. |
| `STP_MESHBLOCK_ABS` | Geocoded meshblock. | Deterministic row-based code. |

For person-week or person-employer-week analysis, geography should be selected
through an explicit rule. Examples include main-job geography, latest-observed
geography, or only retaining geography when all employers agree.

## ETP variables

The extended ETP table contains:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `BN` | Payer business identifier. |
| `DUMMY_FLAG` | Synthetic/dummy identifier flag. |
| `EMPLOYEE_KEY` | Job identifier. |
| `ETP_PMT_DT` | ETP payment date. |
| `ETP_PMT_TYP_CD` | ETP payment type code. |
| `ETP_TAX_FREE_AMT` | Tax-free ETP amount. |
| `ETP_TAX_WHELD_TOTL_AMT` | Total tax withheld from the ETP. |
| `ETP_TXBL_CMPNT_AMT` | Taxable component amount. |
| `LATEST` | Latest-record flag. |
| `PYRL_FNCL_YR` | Payroll financial year. |
| `SEQUENCE_KEY` | ETP sequence key. |
| `SYNTHETIC_AEUID` | Person identifier. |

ETP amounts are separate from ordinary pay-event gross. Downstream analysis
should treat them as termination-related payment components.

## Recommended downstream derivations

The raw generator does not write these derived variables. They are included
here to guide downstream code and naming.

### Event-level semantic components

```r
events_derived <- pay_events |>
  mutate(
    gross_salary_wages = coalesce(INCM_GRS_AMT, 0),
    gross_payment_summary = coalesce(PMT_SUMRY_TOTL_GRS_PMT_AMT, 0),
    allowances = coalesce(ALWNC_INCM_TOTL_AMT, 0),
    gross_plus_allowances = gross_salary_wages + allowances,

    leave_lump_sum_a = coalesce(ANL_LNG_SRVC_UNSD_LS_A_AMT, 0),
    leave_lump_sum_b = coalesce(ANL_LNG_SRVC_UNSD_LS_B_AMT, 0),
    leave_lump_sum = leave_lump_sum_a + leave_lump_sum_b,
    redundancy_lump_sum = coalesce(ANL_LNG_SRVC_UNSD_LS_D_AMT, 0),
    backpay_lump_sum = coalesce(ANL_LNG_SRVC_UNSD_LS_E_AMT, 0),
    lump_sum_total = leave_lump_sum + redundancy_lump_sum + backpay_lump_sum,

    special_income_total =
      coalesce(INCM_LABR_HIR_ARNGMT_GRS_AMT, 0) +
      coalesce(INCM_VA_GRS_AMT, 0) +
      coalesce(INCM_WHM_GRS_AMT, 0) +
      coalesce(INCM_CMNTY_DEV_EMPLT_PRJCT_AMT, 0) +
      coalesce(OTHR_SPCFD_TOTL_AMT, 0) +
      coalesce(INCM_OTHR_AMT, 0),

    foreign_income_total =
      coalesce(F_EMPLT_INCM_GRS_AMT, 0) +
      coalesce(F_EMPLT_INCM_JPDA_GRS_AMT, 0) +
      coalesce(F_INCM_EXMT_AMT, 0),

    tax_withheld = coalesce(TAX_WHELD_TOTL_AMT, 0),
    sg_employer = coalesce(SG_EMPLR_CNTRBTN_AMT, 0),
    reportable_super = coalesce(PYR_SPNTN_CNTRBTN_RPRTBL_AMT, 0),
    reportable_fringe_benefits =
      coalesce(RFB_EXMT_AMT, 0) + coalesce(RFB_TXBL_AMT, 0),

    has_lump_sum = lump_sum_total > 0,
    has_special_income = special_income_total > 0,
    has_termination = !is.na(PYR_PYE_RLTNSHP_CESTN_DT) |
      coalesce(PYR_PYE_RLTNSHP_TRMNTD_IND, 0) == 1
  )
```

### Person-employer-week candidates

Useful person-employer-week columns include:

- `synthetic_aeuid`
- `employer_bn`
- `week_ending`
- `gross_salary_wages_week`
- `allowances_week`
- `gross_plus_allowances_week`
- `gross_payment_summary_week`
- `leave_lump_sum_week`
- `redundancy_lump_sum_week`
- `backpay_lump_sum_week`
- `special_income_total_week`
- `foreign_income_total_week`
- `tax_withheld_week`
- `sg_employer_week`
- `reportable_super_week`
- `reportable_fringe_benefits_week`
- `has_lump_sum_week`
- `has_special_income_week`
- `has_termination_week`
- `pay_event_rows`
- `covered_days`

For accrual-style earnings, allocate `gross_salary_wages` across the overlap
between the pay period and the target week. For cash-flow analysis, allocate
payment and withholding to the week containing `PMT_DT`.

### Person-week candidates

Useful person-week columns include:

- `all_jobs_gross_salary_wages_week`
- `all_jobs_gross_plus_allowances_week`
- `main_job_employer_bn`
- `main_job_gross_salary_wages_week`
- `secondary_jobs_gross_salary_wages_week`
- `n_paid_employers_week`
- `multiple_jobholder_week`
- `any_lump_sum_week`
- `any_special_income_week`
- `any_termination_week`
- `regular_gross_earnings_week`

For earnings analysis, a transparent main-job rule is the employer with the
largest weekly gross salary and wages. Do not use latest employer as the
default main-job rule unless the research question is about employment status
rather than earnings.

## Relationship to AWE and AWOTE

The ABS Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) and Average Weekly Ordinary Time Earnings
(AWOTE) series are survey-based earnings concepts with scope and processing
rules that are not replicated by Phase 1 STP.

The STP product can approximate:

- all-paid-jobs weekly gross salary and wages;
- all-paid-jobs weekly gross plus allowances;
- main-job weekly gross salary and wages;
- multiple jobholding;
- payment-week shocks;
- final-payment and lump-sum flags;
- broad remuneration proxies when super and fringe benefits are added
  separately and labelled carefully.

The STP product cannot cleanly identify:

- ordinary-time earnings;
- overtime earnings;
- hours paid or hourly wages;
- full-time adult ordinary-time scope;
- true bonuses and commissions;
- salary-sacrifice-inclusive cash earnings;
- ABS seasonally adjusted or trend AWE series.

Recommended labels:

| Label | Use? | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `gross_salary_wages_week` | Yes | Directly tied to Phase 1 gross salary and wage fields. |
| `regular_gross_earnings_week` | Yes, if the filter is explicit. | Useful after excluding lump sums, special streams, and final-pay weeks. |
| `all_jobs_weekly_earnings` | Yes, if the component is explicit. | Person-level all-jobs measure. |
| `main_job_weekly_earnings` | Yes, if the main-job rule is explicit. | Main-job analogue, not an ABS survey measure. |
| `awote_week` | No | STP lacks ordinary-time, full-time, adult, and survey-design components. |
| `ote_week` | No | Ordinary-time earnings are not separately observed. |
| `bonus_week` | No | Phase 1 does not separately observe bonuses and commissions. |
| `irregular_payment_week` | Yes, with caveats. | Can flag lump sums, backpay, final payments, corrections, or statistical payment spikes. |

## Validation checks

The STP tests should continue to check both table shape and value semantics.
The current focused test is `tests/testthat/test-dil-2026.R`.

Required shape checks:

- every generated STP table directory exists for the tested month or financial
  year;
- generated columns match `inst/plida_metadata/variables.csv`;
- STP stays parquet-only.

Required amount-semantics checks:

- `INCM_GRS_AMT` equals `PMT_SUMRY_TOTL_GRS_PMT_AMT` for current ordinary
  employee rows;
- `F_EMPLT_INCM_GRS_AMT`, `F_EMPLT_INCM_TOTL_AMT`,
  `F_EMPLT_INCM_TAX_CR_WHELD_AMT`, and `F_EMPLT_INCM_TAX_PMT_AMT` are zero
  unless a foreign-employment stream is explicitly modelled;
- `CNTRCTR_BN` is missing unless a contractor-style stream is explicitly
  modelled;
- `ANL_LNG_SRVC_UNSD_LS_A_AMT` is positive only on final-pay rows with a
  relationship cessation date;
- `ANL_LNG_SRVC_UNSD_LS_A_CD` is present only when lump sum A is positive and
  uses valid lump-sum A codes;
- negative correction rows have negative gross and non-positive withholding,
  but do not create negative foreign-employment amounts;
- gross-payment spikes are represented inside gross fields, not in lump-sum
  fields.

Behavioural checks:

- most positive pay-event rows are fortnightly;
- monthly rows are present and fewer than fortnightly rows;
- weekly rows are present and fewer than monthly rows;
- irregular/chaotic pay periods are present;
- long periods ending near 30 June are present;
- high gross-payment spikes are overrepresented in June relative to the
  underlying pay-event month mix;
- zero, positive, and overlapping job gaps are all present;
- overpayment rows have matching negative correction rows.

## Promotion path

If this note becomes user-facing, the least disruptive path is:

1. Move or copy this file to `vignettes/stp-dataset-explainer.qmd`.
2. Add any package-level vignette dependencies to `DESCRIPTION`.
3. Decide whether to include executable validation chunks or keep the document
   as a static explainer.
4. Add a rendered article route if the package later uses a website or
   `pkgdown`.
5. Keep the raw field interpretation synchronized with
   `tests/testthat/test-dil-2026.R` so documentation and generated data do not
   drift.
